why: A turn range-versus-range spot with chips left for a real river bet. OOP continues wide; IP is tighter and weighted. The frozen public-tree pass is the practical turn solver. Construction, rank-cache fill, training, and evaluation are separate clocks, so this case shows which part of a turn solve dominates.
study_inputs_note: Ranges are study inputs for this benchmark. They are not a solved preflop equilibrium. The queen-high turn is two-tone (Qc 2c), so some rivers complete a club flush and change the betting.
memory_note: 2048 is the engine allocation budget (--memory-mib), not an operating-system limit and not process RSS. The street default is 1024 MiB.
eval_interval_source: --accuracy 0.001 hardcodes eval_interval to 20. There is no flag to change that cadence.
betting_note: One shared bet size (0.5) and one explicit raise size (0.75) on the turn and the river. Per-street bet flags are omitted on purpose: a non-empty per-street bet list is copied onto that street's raises and the shared raise flags are then ignored. All-in is offered as its own action.
